newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will discuss several economic issues, including U.S. sanctions, when he makes an official two-day visit to Burma starting on Friday. Informed sources say that all government and security agencies will hold a final round of discussions today to finalise the premier's agenda with top Burmese junta leaders, including General Than Shwe, General Maung Aye and General Khin Nyunt. (THE NATION)

- The Forestry Department is ready to accept a draft bill to allow communities a role in managing resources in the nation's forests. Up to now, the department has opposed the basic principle on the basis of community activities and populations can not be controlled and forests will suffer. A public hearing scheduled for tomorrow is expected to see attempts to settle contentious issues in the draft. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Ministry of Public Health says it is unable to control the increasing misuse of acupuncture for weight loss. It says that due to legal loopholes, there is no control over the fees charged for medical services, which vary according to individual market strategies. (BANGKOK POST)

- A tax on luxury goods is likely to be boosted to generate 30 billion baht to offset a state revenue shortfall tipped to swell to 88 billion by the end of the fiscal year. The prime minister said yesterday the measure was being considered because it would not hurt the majority. General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh declined to reveal the extent of the hike or the goods to be affected, saying details were being worked out. (BANGKOK POST)

- An economic advisor to Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has called on the Bank of Thailand (BOT) to lower interest rates by 2 percent to stimulate the economy now that the key economic indicators, especially the current account deficit and inflation, are showing signs of improvement. (BUSINESS DAY)
